Executed from a clean checkout of this exact head in a fresh worktree (`npm install` from the committed lockfile, then):

#### Finding 3 — no intended content was dropped from either side of the original conflict
Compared against the pre-merge parents of `e588570` (single parent `a6c71e0e37ed0b5b895f919815af864eee17fcc9`) and against the conflicted `origin/master` text:

- **`AppLayout.tsx`** — reconciled to a single shell rather than a pick-one-side. The pre-conflict `a6c71e0` version (80 lines) had its own hardcoded header (`⚡ SMART FACTORY` / `Operator Dashboard` badge), an inline sidebar and its own `navItems` array. This PR replaces that duplication with the design-system `Header` (which itself renders `StatusBadge`, l.73) and `Sidebar` (which owns the main nav **plus** the 9-module grouped navigation, l.23-45), keeping the skip-to-content link and the `id="main-content"` / `role="main"` landmark that the old version provided. The file's own header comment states the intent explicitly: "Single-shell reconciliation of #149 (design-system Header/Sidebar with 9-module navigation) and #153 (AppLayout wrapper, StatusBadge, incident routes): AppLayout owns the page frame and delegates the header and the sidebar to the design-system components, so the two features never render competing headers/sidebars." Both sides' features are present; only the duplicated chrome is removed.
- **`App.tsx`** — keeps all six routes from the conflicted master text (`/`, `/telemetry`, `/events`, `/incidents`, `/incidents/:incidentId`, plus #255's `/modules/:moduleId`) and the `OverviewPage` index route that the conflict had dropped on one side.
- **`global.css`** — the conflicted master file lost its token block to the marker. This head restores it via `@import '../design-system/tokens.css'` as the single source of truth, and explicitly re-declares only `--shadow-md` and `--shadow-lg` because those two values intentionally differ from the token sheet. **No design token is silently dropped**: `--font-sans`, `--color-bg-primary`, `--color-text-primary`, `--color-primary`, `--color-border` and the rest all resolve through the import, and the page shell now uses the token names (`bg-[var(--color-bg-primary)]`, `text-[var(--color-text-primary)]`) instead of the hardcoded `bg-gray-900 text-gray-100`.
- **`Sidebar.tsx`** — the 9-module navigation survives (`module.path` links, l.152) and the `/incidents` entry is retained alongside `/`, `/telemetry`, `/events`.

#### Finding 4 — scope discipline
`git diff --stat origin/master...decc930f -- dashboard/` touches only dashboard files (8 files, +90/-173). No backend module, contract or build pipeline is modified. The reduction in line count is the removal of duplicated layout chrome, not the removal of features.

**Evidence level:** L1 unit tests + L2 build/typecheck execution in a clean checkout. No browser rendering, no visual regression check, no end-to-end dashboard run. The design-token reconciliation is verified by static analysis of the CSS import chain and by the successful Vite build — not by visual inspection.
